thread:
anya_cs: pinging infra/eng — just got an escalation from a customer (Globex) reporting that after the 2026-11-09 rollout their translation endpoint is returning English-only outputs for Spanish/Korean prompts. customer provided examples and request-ids.

Globex message pasted: 
> Hola — antes del despliegue, cuando pedíamos traducciones a español el modelo devolvía texto en español. Después del despliegue, el modelo responde en Inglés o mezcla english/spanish with bad mixing. Example: input 'Traduce al español: The server is down' -> output 'The server is down' (no translation). Also Korean prompts return romanized or English. This started ~11:10 UTC. Request id: req-3b9f2a.

anya_cs: steps I've done: asked for full request JSON; confirmed they used model 'redwood/open-translate-v2' (hosted), region eu-west; they were on a canary flow for our 2026-11-09 minor rollout (canary id can-20261109-2). They say they saw the issue at 11:10 UTC and again at 11:17.

santiago_eng: thanks, can you paste their minimal reproduce payload?

anya_cs: pasted the payload they sent:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/open-translate-v2",
  "input": "Traduce al español: The server is down",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 200,
  "request_id": "req-3b9f2a"
}
```

anya_cs: also attached a Korean example: input '한국어로 번역: Please reset the router' -> response returned 'Please reset the router' unchanged.

jia_sre: grabbing traces now. do we have the request ids and timestamps?

anya_cs: yes — req-3b9f2a @ 2026-11-09T11:10:23Z, req-7f4b1c @ 2026-11-09T11:17:04Z. I uploaded csv with headers to the incident thread. link: https://paste.redwood.example/gbx-reqs

rollback-bot: Canary can-20261109-2 currently at 30% traffic for redwood/open-translate-v2 in eu-west. No auto-rollback triggered.

oliver_research: quick hypothesis: we changed the system prompt templating in the rollout — there was a PR that normalized language tags at the system prompt layer (to 'English' by default) if locale header missing. If the customer's requests don't include an explicit language header (they used inline 'Traduce al español' in the prompt), the template might have appended 'Language: English' and overshadowed prompt instruction.

santiago_eng: interesting — I remember a change touching prompt-templates for safety. If code appended 'Language: {default_lang}' and default_lang was set to 'en' for this canary, that'll force English.

jia_sre: pulling request traces now. I see both request IDs routed to pool p-eu-2 (shared runtime). Kernel logs show the rendered system prompt for req-3b9f2a: 
```
[rendered_system_prompt]
You are a helpful assistant. Language: English
User instruction: Traduce al español: The server is down
```
so indeed the system prompt contains Language: English.

anya_cs: customer says they were NOT sending any headers like x-redwood-language. they rely on instruction-level language selection. This used to work.

oliver_research: that matches the hypothesis. We likely regressed default behavior: previously we didn't inject a 'Language' directive unless user locale header existed. The rollout change apparently added a default-language injection for safety/consistency. That default should be ignored if user's prompt contains explicit target language tokens. Looks like the renderer order puts the 'Language: English' before the user instruction, and our model obeys that.

santiago_eng: action items: 1) confirm the PR/commit that changed prompt behavior, 2) evaluate if we can hotfix prompt renderer to append language only when user didn't specify any language intent, 3) consider immediate rollback of canary if customer impact is serious.

jia_sre: found PR 8234 merged 2026-11-09 02:03 UTC — title 'prompt-template: normalize language header' by @devops-lex. It sets default_language env var to 'en' in hosted runtime. Can reproduce locally by rendering template with empty header.

santiago_eng: can we reproduce quickly with unit test? oliver, can you run a local render?

oliver_research: reproducer:
```bash
# render with new template
echo '{"user":"Traduce al español: The server is down"}' | ./render_system_prompt --default-lang en
# output:
# You are a helpful assistant. Language: English
# User instruction: Traduce al español: The server is down
```
Model now respects the top-level Language token. Previously default-lang was not injected.

anya_cs: customer impact: Globex uses translations in product flows (billing and status alerts). They flagged 6 customer-facing failures and threaten to pause production calls if not fixed. They are on Dedicated trial but hitting hosted path during canary window. High priority.

rollback-bot: Manual rollback request submitted by santiago_eng — canary can-20261109-2 set to 0% at 2026-11-09T11:28:10Z pending approval.

jia_sre: before we rollback, quick mitigation: I can push a server-side patch to the renderer to detect language keywords in the user's prompt (regex for 'Traduce|traduc|번역|번역해|translate|翻訳') and skip injecting default-language. Patch is small, can roll out to canary-targeted hosts in ~10m. Do we want that instead of full rollback?

santiago_eng: prefer targeted fix first so we don't revert other unrelated improvements. But if more customers surface, we'll rollback. Go ahead with patch to canary hosts.

oliver_research: I'll add a stronger detection for explicit target-language tokens and add unit tests for Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Arabic. Also add a TODO to consider tokenization issues for right-to-left scripts (we didn't change tokenizer).

anya_cs: informed Globex — told them we identified a prompt-template regression, patching canary hosts now, will monitor and follow up in 30 minutes. They want request-level notification once their req-ids are reprocessed or observed fixed.

jia_sre: deployed patch to canary pool p-eu-2 at 11:37 UTC. Monitoring logs show the rendered system prompt now: 
```
You are a helpful assistant.
User instruction: Traduce al español: The server is down
```
so no Language: English injection.

anya_cs: customer confirmed at 11:42 UTC: "I re-ran the same requests, translations now return Spanish as expected. Thank you." :tada:

santiago_eng: follow-ups: 1) revert the default 'en' env in next config and make default-language opt-in, 2) add e2e tests that include instruction-level language detection, 3) add a rollout check that flags prompt-template changes when canary uses shared runtime.

oliver_research: filing PR to revert default injection + tests (PR 8247).

jia_sre: closing loop with ops: will leave canary at 30% for 1 hour while monitoring; if no regressions, we'll resume gradual rollout and ensure customers with multilingual workflows are contacted.

anya_cs: marking as resolved for Globex for now. Will follow up with a postmortem draft and customer-facing post describing root cause and remediation.

santiago_eng: thanks team. good catch on the subtle system-prompt ordering.

rollback-bot: Canary can-20261109-2 status: 30% -> 30% (manual rollback aborted).

anya_cs: filing the customer update: "Root cause: a recent prompt-template change caused a default 'Language: English' header to be injected when no language header was supplied, which overrode inline user instructions. Remediation: hotfix deployed to canary hosts and PR submitted to make default injection opt-in. We will follow up with a formal postmortem."

end of thread
